Act as the analyst on an investment bank's deal team advising a private-equity sponsor on taking the EdTech company KSchool private, and work the engagement through 38 dependent, reactively-unlocked stages built on APEX-Agents 'Investment Banking World 244'. Read the deal documents under /app/world -- the live LBO (LBO model v11.xlsx), DCF (DCF_v11.xlsx) and comps (KSchool - Comps v3.xlsx) workbooks, a precedent-transactions workbook, a public-comps 10-K/8-K library, and an offline market_data pack (U.S. Treasury par curve, a sector P/E and a peer CAGR) -- and answer each stage by rebuilding the relevant model or reading the source filings under a specific set of assumptions. Stages unlock REACTIVELY in a strict order: the next question only appears after you submit a structured answer to the current one, so the long engagement must be worked sequentially. Thirteen stages rebuild the leveraged buyout exactly as the workbook computes it -- its circular revolver/cash-sweep, term-loan amortisation and exit-equity conventions included -- across the base case, a Treasury-priced debt package with full per-year schedules (annual revolver draw/repayment, revolver balance, interest, DSCR), a leverage sweep (with per-case cumulative interest and minimum DSCR), exit-multiple and holding-period sensitivities (with per-horizon cumulative interest), an offer-premium sweep, credit metrics under the Treasury-linked package (min DSCR, exit Debt/EBITDA and Debt/Equity, peak-revolver year, cumulative interest), and a combined scenario (with peak revolver and cumulative interest); six stages require precise recomputation of trading-comp and precedent-transaction multiples (the workbooks' summary cells are rounded) -- means, medians, min/max and a trimmed mean -- chained to KSchool implied valuations; eight stages require opening the actual SEC filings in the public-comps library (PowerSchool and Instructure Q4 earnings releases) to extract line items from the consolidated statements and GAAP-to-non-GAAP reconciliations and recompute multi-year revenue/EBITDA CAGRs, gross and EBITDA margins, non-GAAP operating expenses, free-cash-flow figures and a net-debt bridge; eleven stages re-run the DCF for the real engagement tasks (a revised cost of debt/growth/beta, a four-cell cost-of-capital reset, a peer-anchored revenue CAGR with a six-year projection, peer-anchored R&D/opex CAGRs from the 10-Ks, and an earnings adjustment to a sector P/E) plus replica-verified cost-of-capital/horizon scenarios (a full WACC/valuation build-up with per-year FCF and revenue, two further Treasury-linked resets, and a 7-year horizon extension). Many inputs are derived (leverage x EBITDA, Treasury rate + spread, peer CAGRs) and many outputs are not single cells. Every answer is an exact figure submitted via the `submit` tool and graded deterministically (no LLM judge) within a tight tolerance against a frozen answer key (146 fields).

Act as outside counsel for a law firm juggling four client matters and work them through 70 dependent stages over three realistic, combined legal worlds (APEX 'Law World 433' assisted-living operator + 'Law World 431' MGR/AIAG commercial office lease + 'Law World 434' HarborView HK/Singapore self-storage roll-up) plus an authored litigation-hold document-retrieval matter, ~600 documents total. Stages and their supporting documents unlock REACTIVELY: the next question and its attachments only appear after you submit a structured answer to the current one, so the matters must be worked in order. Matter A spans a wrongful-death suit, a breach-of-contract suit, and a multi-state regulatory compliance review (with two late corrections that force revising an earlier answer); Matter B is a full commercial-lease lifecycle; Matter C is a cross-border M&A roll-up; Matter D is 12 chained-read discovery-production stages, each forcing you to follow a 3-document breadcrumb full of decoys to buried answers. Each stage's free-form investigation ends in a structured `submit` (booleans / numbers / enums / verbatim quotes whose source document you must find yourself) graded deterministically (no LLM judge) against a frozen legal answer key.

Close RTL-to-GDSII signoff on the lowRISC ibex_core CPU for the SkyWater sky130hd PDK using OpenROAD-flow-scripts, ported from the APEX-Agents last-exam task engineering/openroad_sky130_ibex_pnr_signoff. The full ORFS toolchain (OpenROAD/Yosys/KLayout/Magic) and PDK are baked into the image and run natively (no Docker-in-Docker). The agent works eight reactive, dependent stages: from a deliberately-bad starter config.mk it runs the flow, reads the OpenSTA/KLayout/Magic reports, diagnoses each violation (routing-layer stack, floorplan congestion, synthesis/CTS bloat, timing margins), tunes config.mk, and re-runs -- iterating until setup/hold WNS>=0, setup TNS=0, DRC count=0, an LVS verdict is reached, and die area (~290k um2 +/-8%) and power (~23 mW +/-15%) land in budget, all within at most 8 completed full passes (12 max). Stages unlock only as earlier ones are submitted, so the work proceeds in order, and the score is computed deterministically from the REAL ORFS report artifacts (timing/DRC/LVS/area/power, per-pass config snapshots, JOURNAL.md fidelity) -- never from the agent's self-reported numbers.

Play a full game of chess from the standard opening, turn-by-turn through a terminal game server, as White against a bundled superhuman chess engine (Stockfish, node-limited, single-thread, deterministic, ~3000+ Elo). The agent cannot win; it is scored on SURVIVAL -- how long it lasts before being checkmated, normalized to how long a grandmaster-strength reference engine survives against the same opponent (measured live by the referee), with a draw scoring ~0.9 and a checkmate 1.0. The engine and chess library live only in an isolated sidecar container the agent cannot access (no engine, no chess library, no internet), so the agent must calculate every move itself; because full chess is intractable, there is no solvable sub-game or short script to exploit.

Bring up and debug the twosigma/frost RV32GCB SystemVerilog CPU (an out-of-order, Tomasulo-style core): the RTL under hw/rtl has been seeded with an undisclosed number of deliberately-injected bugs spread across the datapath/control AND the out-of-order machinery (rename/RAT, reservation stations, reorder buffer, CDB arbiter, load/store queues + forwarding, branch recovery). There is no bug map: the agent is not told how many bugs there are, which files they live in, or what kind they are. The hard part is LOCALIZATION, not detection -- the symptom a test reports is deliberately far from the root cause (e.g. sub-word loads fail because of the store-to-load forwarding CAM, not the load unit), and several bugs can alias the same symptom. The full FOSS toolchain (Verilator, Yosys, SymbiYosys + Z3/Boolector, RISC-V GCC, cocotb) is baked into the image and runs natively. The agent works eight reactive, dependent stages: build the Verilator model, run the frost test runners, localize each failure by diffing simulator behavior against the golden Spike-derived references, patch the SystemVerilog, and re-run -- iterating until directed riscv-tests, riscv-arch-test compliance signatures, constrained-random torture co-sim, real-application self-checking co-sim, and bounded SymbiYosys formal proofs are all green. Stage briefs name the verification LAYER to get green, never files or defect types. Stages unlock only as earlier ones are submitted, and the score is computed deterministically by REBUILDING the model from the agent's hw/rtl and running the real runners (with a hidden arch-test subset), never from the agent's self-reported numbers; a tamper gate SHA256-checks the read-only harness.

Recover 7 progressively corrupted, genuinely hard variant-Sudoku puzzles (50-54 near-minimal blank cells) turn-by-turn through a terminal game server. Boards layer 2-4 constraint types — diagonal, anti-knight, anti-king, killer cages (cage sums), and thermometers (strictly increasing runs) — and hide 3-6 SUBTLE corrupt givens that are locally consistent (no immediate violation), so detection requires global constraint reasoning. The server hides all solutions and corrupt-cell coordinates, unlocks puzzle k+1 only after puzzle k is server-verified, issues a fresh per-move token (so each fill requires a read-decide round trip), and enforces a real wall-clock floor between accepted moves. Every accepted move is written to an HMAC-chained actions.log; the verifier rejects any log it did not produce and scores by replaying the authenticated actions in a fresh engine.

Sparse inverse-problem marathon with covariate shift on the underlying linear operator. Recover a 200-dim sparse signal X from 50-dim observations Y on a held-out test set whose forward operator is drawn from a different distribution than train/val. Wall cap 60s/run on 1 CPU; submit-time honesty audit detects val-set leakage; back-weighted reward (power 2). The verifier oracle knows the test-time operator, which the agent does not — making oracle effectively unreachable.

Recover the TRUE semantics of an undocumented, legacy-friendly job-config format and repair a buggy config-normalisation engine so it produces correct canonical output on HIDDEN configs -- STAGE BY STAGE. There are NO labelled cases on disk: the agent works through the `cfg` CLI against a persistent daemon, reading a deliberately NOISY, partly-wrong spec (with contradicting revisions that drop as it progresses -- each revision fixes an old lie while sometimes planting a new field-specific one), two free worked examples per stage, and a budgeted, one-at-a-time SAMPLE channel. It repairs /opt/cfg/engine.py and proves each stage by passing many fresh RANDOM probe rounds (`cfg probe`) whose answers are stored only as hashes; five stages unlock in order: A (workers/retries/batch_size) -> B (memory/timeout/disk units) -> C (precision incl int8/log_level incl trace/scheduler) -> D (coupled mem_per_worker_mb & effective_batch, computed from already-resolved A/B/C values) -> E (derived effective_throughput). Every gated call (sample/probe/submit) is TIME-FLOORED and NONCE-chained, and the append-only actions.log is HMAC-chained; the verifier replays the recorded engine snapshots against hidden configs and credits a field only if its stage's STAGE_PASS is present, so full score requires passing all five paced stages. It must infer field aliases & deprecated names, a four-layer precedence chain (explicit > mode preset > base profile > default), defaults, three DISAGREEING unit families (binary memory mb/gb/kb/tb vs decimal disk gb/tb with binary gib/tib, timeout s/m/h/ms/d/w), three-way and five-way enums, interacting fields whose normalisation depends on other resolved values, clamping, and an entangled derived field with undocumented multi-term coefficients.
